name: Measure performance and attribution
summary: After each month end the performance team calculates time-weighted returns net of all costs for every client portfolio and pool, by asset class, strategy and external mandate, compares them with Board-approved benchmarks and explains the difference through attribution. Work starts only when positions are reconciled and prices approved, and the results must agree with fund accounting's signed-off books, so breaks and data errors found late send the cycle back to recalculation. Private assets are carried at last quarter's values until new valuations are approved, which restates earlier months. A second analyst and the manager review before release, because the official returns feed client reports, board reports, manager monitoring and incentive pay.

baseline.org_archetype: A Canadian provincial not-for-profit asset manager with five client portfolios and four pooled funds, a five-person performance team, a vendor performance system fed from the book of record and custodian, and spreadsheets for private assets and restatements.
baseline.notes: Volume of nine cycles a month is five client portfolios plus four pools at end 2021; six in 2020 and ten in 2022.

unit_of_work: one monthly performance cycle for one client portfolio or pool
trigger: Month end, with work starting once reconciled positions and approved prices are released for the portfolio or pool.
end_state: Official returns and attribution for the month are approved, the period is locked and the results are published to users.

volume.seasonality: Every month; the month after quarter-end private valuations are approved carries restatements, and year end adds annual and longer-period figures for the annual report and incentive pay.

evidence.note: Four pools at end 2021 (mgr_ar21) plus five client portfolios from the organisation file.

Organisation file cost on Job Bank NOC 11101 Toronto wages (jobbank_11101); four analysts, about half their time on the monthly cycle and the rest on ad hoc analysis, manager monitoring support and system work.
Organisation file cost on NOC 10010 wages (jobbank_10010); share of time is an author estimate.
Organisation file cost; benchmark and reference data work for performance is an author estimate.

systems.name: Order management, pre-trade compliance and investment book of record platform (vendor software as a service)
Custodian portal (custody, accounting records, net asset value reports, cash and corporate action notices)
Market data terminals and vendor feeds (prices, indices, reference data)
Private markets investment accounting and monitoring system (commitments, calls, distributions, valuations)
Investment data warehouse and business intelligence reports
Email, video calls and collaboration suite

steps.name: Confirm month-end data readiness
steps.description: The performance analyst checks the close tracker for the portfolio or pool: positions and cash reconciled to the custodian, month-end prices approved, corporate actions and trades for the month booked in the book of record. Performance runs cannot start on positions that still have open breaks.

error.defect_description: Load started before a late trade correction was booked.

evidence.note: External manager reconciliations typically arrive on business days 3 to 5 and month-end close targets run from business day 5 to 15 (nmerb_ps); the model manager is assumed to release reconciled positions around business day 3 to 5.

steps.name: Load month-end holdings, transactions and cash flows
steps.description: The overnight interface loads the month's positions, transactions, income and external cash flows from the book of record and custodian files into the performance system for every account in the portfolio or pool.

error.defect_description: Account mapping or a new security missing from the interface.

evidence.note: Performance books of record are built from custodian and accounting data feeds (prim_rfp). Timing is an author estimate.

steps.name: Check load completeness and interface exceptions
steps.description: An investment data analyst reviews the load report: record counts against the book of record, unmapped accounts or securities, missing prices and cash flows without a type, and fixes what can be fixed in reference data.

error.defect_description: An unmapped account is left out of a composite.

next.condition: exceptions need a fix and reload

evidence.note: Maintaining data integrity for calculations is the top performance challenge for 54% of firms (cutter_pma2025). Exception rate is an author estimate.

steps.name: Fix mapping or reference data and reload
steps.description: The data analyst sets up the missing security or account mapping, corrects the cash flow classification with operations and asks technology to rerun the interface, then re-checks the load.

error.defect_description: Classification fixed for one month but not back-dated.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Load and validate benchmark returns
steps.description: The data analyst loads month-end index returns and constituents from the index providers, rebuilds each client's blended policy benchmark from its current policy weights and each pool's strategy benchmark, and compares the results with vendor terminal values.

error.defect_description: Blended benchmark built with superseded policy weights.

control.basis: The model manager benchmark policy: only Board-approved benchmarks and client policy weights are used

evidence.note: Benchmarks are researched by Risk, recommended by the Management Investment Committee and approved by the Board (mgr_ar22) and must reflect the mandate (gips_ao 21.A.15). Times are author estimates.

steps.name: Chase the index provider for missing or revised data
steps.description: The data analyst raises a ticket with the index provider for a missing return, a late constituent file or a revised index level, and waits for the corrected file before rebuilding the affected benchmarks.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Calculate returns
steps.description: The performance system calculates daily time-weighted returns for every account, strategy, pool, asset class and the total portfolio, geometrically linked to monthly and longer periods, gross and net of external manager fees.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: The model manager reports time-weighted returns net of all costs based on daily calculations (mgr_ar20); monthly valuation and geometric linking (gips_ao 22.A.20, 22.A.21).

steps.name: Review return outliers and tolerance exceptions
steps.description: The performance analyst reviews the exception report: accounts whose return differs from their benchmark or from the external manager's own reported return by more than tolerance, large cash flows, negative market values and returns that differ from the prior preliminary run.

error.defect_description: An outlier is accepted as market-driven when it is a data error.

evidence.note: Performance calculations need review against third-party records (aca_perf); errors occur even with tight controls (cfa_errors). Outlier rate is an author estimate.

steps.name: Investigate and correct the outlier
steps.description: The analyst traces the outlier to its cause, typically a missing or stale price, a cash flow booked on the wrong date, an unprocessed corporate action or a fee accrual, gets the record corrected by reconciliations or accounting and requests a recalculation.

error.defect_description: Correction fixes the symptom in performance only, not in the book of record.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Reconcile performance values and flows to the accounting package
steps.description: Once fund accounting signs off the month, the analyst compares ending market values, income and external cash flows in the performance system with the signed-off NAV package for each account and pool, and lists differences above tolerance.

error.defect_description: Timing difference accepted that is a real break.

control.basis: Performance measurement procedures: official returns use values and flows that agree to the signed-off accounting book of record

evidence.note: Custody standards treat variances above 10 basis points of NAV as needing explanation (nmerb_ps); reconciliation to authoritative records is a baseline control objective (sifma_soc1). Wait for the accounting sign-off and break rate are author estimates.

steps.name: Resolve the break with fund accounting
steps.description: A fund accountant explains or corrects each difference, often an accrual posted after the performance load, a late private market booking or a pool unit transaction in the wrong period. If data changed, returns are recalculated.

error.defect_description: Correction made in accounting but not reloaded to performance.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Apply cost accruals to produce net-of-cost returns
steps.description: The analyst loads the month's the model manager cost recovery accruals and external manager fee accruals by pool and client portfolio from the accounting package, applies them to produce returns net of all costs, and compares the cost drag with prior months.

error.defect_description: Quarterly fee accrual applied in full to one month.

evidence.note: The model manager reports returns net of all costs (mgr_ar22); net-of-fees returns deduct external fees and investment management costs (gips_ao 22.A.24).

steps.name: Roll forward private asset values for cash flows
steps.description: For private holdings without a new valuation the analyst carries the last approved quarter-end value forward, adjusted for the month's capital calls and distributions, and checks the private markets system totals against the accounting package.

error.defect_description: Distribution treated as income instead of a return of capital.

evidence.note: Private equity returns use the latest partnership valuations, typically lagging one quarter, adjusted for cash flows (prim_rfp); estimated values must be the best approximation (gips_ao 22.A.18).

steps.name: Check for newly approved quarterly private valuations
steps.description: The analyst checks whether the valuation committee approved quarter-end private values since the last cycle. If so, the months since that quarter end must be recalculated and restated.

error.defect_description: Approval missed, restatement deferred a month.

next.condition: new valuations approved for this portfolio or pool

evidence.note: Fund reports arrive about 60 days after quarter end (ilpa_faq) and the insurance client reviews non-traded values quarterly (iclient_if); only client portfolios and private pools are affected, so about one cycle in five carries a restatement (author estimate).

steps.name: Load approved valuations and recompute prior months
steps.description: The analyst loads the approved quarter-end values, replaces the rolled-forward estimates and recalculates returns for the quarter-end month and the months since, at holding, asset class and total portfolio level.

error.defect_description: One holding's valuation applied to the wrong owning account.

evidence.note: When estimated values are used the asset owner must assess the difference to the final value and adjust when it is received (22.A.18).

steps.name: Quantify the restatement and assess materiality
steps.description: The manager reviews the size of the change to each month's total portfolio and asset class returns against the restatement policy thresholds, decides how it is disclosed to clients and the board, and records it in the restatement log.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: Performance restatement and error correction policy (materiality thresholds, disclosure to clients and the board)

evidence.note: Firms set absolute materiality thresholds of 11 to 50 basis points and log errors (cfa_errors); material errors are corrected and reported to the oversight body (gips_ao 21.A.16).

steps.name: Notify users of restated months
steps.description: The analyst sends the restatement memo to client reporting, the relevant investment teams and risk, so monthly and quarterly reports can show the bridge from reported to restated figures.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Run attribution
steps.description: The analyst runs attribution of the portfolio's excess return over its benchmark: for client portfolios by asset class allocation against policy weights and selection within each asset class; for pools by region, sector or external manager; with currency and overlay effects shown separately.

error.defect_description: Holding classified to the wrong asset class, distorting allocation and selection.

evidence.note: Attribution at total fund, asset class, sub asset class, manager and security level (prim_rfp); net value added against IPS benchmarks (mgr_ar22). Times are author estimates.

steps.name: Review attribution residuals and explain drivers
steps.description: The analyst checks that the effects add up to the excess return with a small residual, investigates large residuals from cash flow timing or classification, and writes short explanations of the main contributors for the package.

error.defect_description: Explanation contradicts the attribution numbers.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Prepare the performance package and checklist
steps.description: The analyst assembles returns by period, benchmark returns, value added, attribution and restatement notes into the standard package and completes the monthly sign-off checklist with links to the reconciliations.

error.defect_description: Package shows a pre-correction figure.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Second analyst reviews the package
steps.description: A second performance analyst who did not prepare the package re-performs key checks: total portfolio return against the sum of its parts, reconciliation tie-outs, benchmark construction and restatements, and returns errors to the preparer.

error.defect_description: Error missed in review.

control.basis: Maker-checker review of official returns before release

evidence.note: Unreviewed spreadsheet changes and single-person ownership are common failure points (aca_perf). Error share is an author estimate.

steps.name: Manager approves official returns
steps.description: The manager of performance reviews the package, questions unusual results and restatements, and approves the month's official returns, which then become the figures used for client reports, board reports, manager monitoring and incentive pay.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: Performance results approval before release; official returns also drive incentive compensation

evidence.note: The model manager's controls were covered by a SOC 1 Type 2 from October 2021 (mgr_ar22); account performance is an optional SOC 1 area (sifma_soc1). Rework share is an author estimate.

steps.name: Lock the period in the performance system
steps.description: The analyst locks the month in the performance system so approved returns cannot be changed without a logged reopening approved by the manager.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: SOC 1 IT general controls over logical access and change management of approved performance data

evidence.note: Logical security and change management are baseline SOC 1 IT general control areas (sifma_soc1).

steps.name: Publish results and notify users
steps.description: The analyst publishes approved results to the data warehouse and emails client reporting, investment teams, risk and finance that the month is final, attaching the package and any restatement notice.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Answer user queries on released results
steps.description: The analyst answers questions from portfolio managers, client reporting or relationship managers about a return, benchmark or attribution effect. Occasionally the query reveals an error, and a corrected package goes back through review and approval.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

exceptions.name: Interface load exceptions
exceptions.description: New securities, unmapped accounts or unclassified cash flows stop a clean load; data management fixes reference data and reloads.

exceptions.name: Missing or revised benchmark data
exceptions.description: An index provider's file is late or revised, so benchmarks are rebuilt after the corrected file arrives.

exceptions.name: Return outlier from a data error
exceptions.description: A stale price, mis-dated cash flow or unprocessed corporate action produces an outlier; data is corrected and returns recalculated.

exceptions.name: Break with the accounting package
exceptions.description: Performance values or flows disagree with signed-off accounting; fund accounting explains or corrects and returns may be recalculated.

exceptions.name: Restatement from new private valuations
exceptions.description: Approved quarter-end private values replace rolled-forward estimates, restating earlier months; the manager assesses materiality and users are notified.

exceptions.name: Correction after release
exceptions.description: A user query reveals an error in released returns; the package is corrected, reviewed and re-approved.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from month end to approved official returns
benchmarks.population: Derived from public pension custody service levels for monthly performance

evidence.note: Preliminary monthly performance within 10 business days, final before next month end (ocers_qa); performance 5 business days after a close that runs to business day 5 to 15 (nmerb_ps). Ten business days is about 14 calendar days; p90 is an author estimate.

benchmarks.population: Custody services RFP of a US county public pension system, 2022

benchmarks.unit: business days after the month-end close
benchmarks.population: Custody bank performance standards of a US state educational retirement board, 2024

evidence.note: The same standard counts a performance revision above 5 basis points from custodian error as a failure.

benchmarks.population: CFA Institute survey of 146 GIPS-compliant firms

evidence.note: Relative thresholds of 5% to 10% are used alongside.

benchmarks.population: Cutter Associates performance measurement and attribution survey, 42 firms

evidence.note: Survey is from 2025, after the reference period.

pain_points.description: Data quality problems (missing prices, mis-dated cash flows, unmapped securities) are found only when returns look wrong, forcing recalculation late in the cycle.

evidence.note: 54% of firms name data integrity for calculations as a top challenge.

pain_points.description: Performance and accounting hold separate copies of values and flows, so a late accounting adjustment creates breaks and reruns.

evidence.note: Author estimate based on separate performance and accounting systems in the organisation file.

pain_points.description: Private asset values lag a quarter and are restated when approved, so the team recomputes past months and every report needs a bridge.

evidence.note: One-quarter lag for private equity and adjustment when final values arrive.

pain_points.description: Restatements, private roll-forwards and attribution commentary live in spreadsheets maintained by one or two people, a key-person and unreviewed-change risk.

evidence.note: Spreadsheet templates with unrecorded changes and single-person ownership.

assumptions: Nine cycles a month: five client portfolios and four pools at end 2021. Pool cycles are simpler (public assets, no private restatements), so per-case times are an average of the two kinds.
The model manager calculates performance in-house on a vendor system fed from its book of record and the custodian; its exact system and timetable are not published.
The case starts at month end; waiting for reconciled positions (s01) and the accounting sign-off (s10) is modelled as waits, not as upstream steps.
Restatements affect about one cycle in five: client portfolios and any private pool in the month after quarter-end valuations are approved.
Interface shares give the share of months in which each input is usually the last to arrive; every cycle uses all of them except client service requests, which add ad hoc reruns.
Official returns also drive incentive pay, which is why approval sits with the manager and a second analyst reviews every package.

Loaded hourly costs are from the organisation file. Stated FTE (2.8) is about twice the hands-on time implied by nine cycles a month, because analysts also answer ad hoc requests, support manager monitoring, maintain benchmarks and test system changes, which are not modelled here.

sources.title: The model manager 2020 Annual Report
sources.supports: New client reporting suite in 2020 with a core set of concise reports for all clients; quarterly performance recaps, positioning and commentary; KPI framework; a consistent core team for client management teams and investment committees; cost allocation policy and guidelines for fair, consistent allocation to the model manager products, segregated assets and clients, overseen by a Cost Allocation Committee; tiered approval authorities; costs reported regularly to senior management, the Finance and Audit Committee and clients; returns net of all costs, time-weighted, based on daily calculations; total benchmark daily weighted by clients' investment in each strategy; 2020 total costs $384.3 million (55.3 cents per $100).

sources.title: The model manager 2021 Annual Report
sources.supports: Clean SOC 1 Type I report on the design of controls as at 30 September 2021, with Type II planned for 2022; Board and client reporting redesigned in 2021 including a Quarterly Risk Insights report; full cost recovery without profit; the model manager allocates to and recovers all operational costs from clients based on agreed cost allocation principles; 2021 total costs $473.7 million (63.1 cents per $100 of AUM), investment management costs $317.2 million, operating expenses $156.5 million; recovery of costs revenue $216.6 million; year-end receivable from clients for cost recoveries $36.6 million plus HST (2020: $17.7 million); external fees paid as agent and collected from clients; amounts collected in advance held as deferred recovery of costs; financial statements authorised by the Board on 24 February 2022; CEM benchmarking of costs.

sources.title: The model manager 2022 Annual Report
sources.supports: Inaugural SOC 1 Type 2 report with a clean opinion that controls were designed and operated effectively from 1 October 2021 to 30 September 2022; returns net of all costs using the time-weighted rate of return; benchmark policy under which Risk researches and reviews benchmarks, the Management Investment Committee recommends them and the Board approves them; net value added defined against the IPS benchmark; interim private markets administration software and a new risk and total portfolio system implemented in 2022.

sources.title: Insurance fund (The insurance client web page with the statement of investment policies)
sources.supports: The model manager is sole investment manager; fund performance, risk and compliance are reviewed at least quarterly and the model manager's performance annually; liquidity monitored at least monthly; fair value estimates for non-traded investments made at least annually and reviewed at least quarterly, with third-party valuations checked for reasonableness by the model manager; the model manager establishes strategy benchmarks and must advise the insurance client of total fund benchmark changes.

sources.title: Asset Manager's Guide to SOC 1 (June 2017)
sources.publisher: SIFMA Asset Management Group and Grant Thornton
sources.supports: Baseline asset manager SOC 1 scope including reconciliation and client reporting; baseline control objective that account statements reflect the correct holdings and market value and are provided to clients in a complete and timely manner; reconciliation objective that discrepancies are researched and resolved timely; account performance listed as not baseline and fee calculation and billing as another area to consider; IT general controls over job scheduling, logical access and change management.

sources.title: 2020 GIPS Standards for Asset Owners
sources.supports: Time-weighted returns required for total funds; valuation at least monthly, at month end and on large cash flows; monthly returns geometrically linked; private market investments valued and returns calculated at least quarterly; when preliminary or estimated values are used the difference to the final value must be assessed and adjusted when the final value arrives (22.A.18); net-of-fees returns deduct transaction costs, external fees and investment management costs (22.A.24); material errors must be corrected and corrected reports given to the oversight body (21.A.16); benchmarks must reflect the mandate; reports to oversight bodies updated within 12 months of each annual period end.

sources.title: Cutter reveals findings from Performance Measurement and Attribution Benchmarking Survey (news release)
sources.supports: 42 firms with USD 7.2 trillion AUM: 54% name maintaining data integrity for calculations and meeting demand for more frequent and detailed reporting as top challenges; 48% satisfied with their performance solution; reliance on manual workarounds that contribute to operational errors; 61% plan a new performance system within two years.

sources.title: How do firms treat errors in investment performance?
sources.supports: Survey of 146 GIPS-compliant firms: most use a two-part materiality test with absolute thresholds of 11 to 50 basis points and relative thresholds of 5% to 10%; 78% keep an Excel error-correction log; 59% have a formal committee that reviews errors; errors occur even with tight controls.

sources.title: Operational challenges with performance calculation and reporting
sources.supports: Performance calculations often rely on spreadsheet templates whose changes go unrecorded or unreviewed; key-person risk when one employee owns the models; responsibility split across fund accounting, investor relations, analytics and compliance; many managers lack written policies for performance calculation and review.

sources.title: Request for Proposals: Investment Performance Reporting Services
sources.publisher: Massachusetts Pension Reserves Investment Management Board (PRIM)
sources.supports: Scope for a public pension investment manager's performance reporting: monthly and quarterly packages from the custodian performance book of record; gross and net of fee returns at account, asset class and total fund level; benchmark comparison; attribution at total fund, asset class, sub asset class, manager and security level; custom benchmarks and composites. Sample report notes: private equity returns use the latest partnership valuations, typically lagging one calendar quarter, adjusted for cash flows; property and timber benchmarks lagged one quarter because they are published 25 days after quarter end.

sources.title: Custody Services RFP: Questions and Answers (October 2022)
sources.supports: Preliminary monthly performance report covering benchmark, portfolio and composite performance required no later than ten business days after month end; finalized performance report must be issued before the next month end.

sources.title: Custody Bank RFP, Appendix F: Performance Standards and Related Key Performance Indicators
sources.supports: Month-end close targets: 5th business day for externally managed and cash accounts, 10th for internally managed and commingled funds, 15th for alternative investment accounts; external manager position reconciliations typically received on business days 3 to 5; variances above 10 basis points of NAV explained; performance reporting due 5 business days after the month-end close; a performance revision above 5 basis points from custodian error counts as a failure; asset servicing invoices within 60 days of period end.

sources.title: ILPA Reporting Template and ILPA Performance Templates: Frequently Asked Questions (January 2025)
sources.supports: Suggested delivery timeline, deferring to fund documents: direct funds 60 days after quarter end and 120 days after fiscal year end; funds of funds 120 and 180 days.
